title: Reconstruction of operadic sections from coherent colored operations
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functor categories, full subcategories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and the definitions of symmetric infinity-operads and relative algebra categories in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping]. Fix sufficiently large universes. Let $O$ be a small ordinary symmetric colored operad: it has a set of colors, sets of operations with each finite labeled list of inputs and one output, permutation actions, unary identities, and associative unital equivariant substitution; nullary operations are allowed. Write $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $\mathrm{Fin}_*$ have these finite pointed sets as objects and pointed maps as arrows. Its category of operators $O^\otimes$ has finite tuples of colors as objects. An arrow over $f:\langle n\rangle\to\langle k\rangle$ is one operation $(c_i)_{f(i)=j}\to d_j$ for each $j\ne *$; discarded inputs contribute no operation. Composition is substitution. Let $q:E^\otimes\to N(O^\otimes)$ be a cocartesian fibration which is a map of infinity-operads. For a color $c$, write $E_c$ for the degreewise fibre over the one-term tuple $(c)$. Suppose inert projections identify $E^\otimes_{(c_1,\ldots,c_n)}\simeq\prod_i E_{c_i}$, including the empty product. For an operation $\theta:(c_1,\ldots,c_r)\to d$, denote its transport functor by $T_\theta:\prod_iE_{c_i}\to E_d$.

Inert-preserving sections of $q$ can be reconstructed from the following data, and restriction to these data is an equivalence of infinity-categories. Choose $x_c\in E_c$ for each color and a structure arrow $T_\theta(x_{c_1},\ldots,x_{c_r})\to x_d$ for each operation. For unary identity operations this is the identity equivalence under $T_{1_c}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{E_c}$. Require that the associated total arrows over inert operators are $q$-cocartesian, compatibly with their compositions; the structure arrows displayed above lie in the target color fibre, whereas the associated total arrows are obtained by preceding them with the chosen transport lifts. Include the identity and permutation compatibilities and all homotopy coherent substitution compatibilities: for each finite rooted tree labeled by operations, all comparison simplices between evaluating its vertices successively and evaluating any contractions of its inner edges, compatible with further contractions, grafting and insertion of unary identities. A nullary vertex uses the empty-input transport. These compatibilities are data in the mapping spaces, not merely equalities in a homotopy category. Coherences for a forest are the products of those for its output trees, pulled back along the corresponding projections of the external inputs; inputs sent to the basepoint are omitted.

The reconstructed section has value $(x_{c_1},\ldots,x_{c_n})$ under the Segal equivalence. Its arrow over $f$ has output $j$ equal to the structure arrow of the operation on $f^{-1}(j)$; its composition simplices are the specified substitution simplices. A transformation is reconstructed from maps of the color objects and the compatible operation-naturality simplices and all higher substitution compatibilities. The same reconstruction holds with arbitrary simplicial parameter $K$: color objects are functors $K\to E_c$, operation arrows are coherent transformations, and the higher compatibility data are parameterized over $K$. It commutes with restrictions in $K$, restriction to suboperads, and projection to any chosen colors. The space of reconstructions equipped with their identification with the specified data is contractible. This assertion imposes no limit, colimit, or presentability hypothesis.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Construction 2.1.1.7, Definition 2.1.1.10, Example 2.1.1.21 and Definition 2.1.3.1 and Remark 2.1.3.4; coherent outputwise reconstruction formulation of the operator-category Segal axioms. Source inspected online; WANTED archive in literature/. No Stacks tag treats infinity-operadic coherent sections.

proof.text:
Put $B=N(O^\otimes)$ and write $\Gamma_I(q)$ for the full category of inert-preserving sections, using only the relative-algebra definition in [lem-coef-relative-operadic-terminal-active-mapping]. Choose $X_{\mathbf c}$ over each tuple, together with its identification with $(x_{c_i})_i$ under the assumed Segal equivalence. A quasi-inverse, unit and counit identify the space of each such choice with a point. Apply [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-mapping] to $q$ and its chosen coherent transports. For an operator $f:\mathbf c\to\mathbf d$ with output operations $\theta_j$, it gives
$$M_f(X_{\mathbf c},X_{\mathbf d})\simeq\prod_j\operatorname{Map}_{E_{d_j}}\bigl(T_{\theta_j}((x_{c_i})_{f(i)=j}),x_{d_j}\bigr).$$
The comparison uses the actual inert projections and transport triangles; the empty target is terminal and a nullary input block contributes its displayed factor.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7; Definition 2.1.1.10(1)-(3), especially its mapping-space condition; Remark 2.1.1.14. The relative mapping-space calculation is written out here.

proof.text: The comparison in step 1 is a complete coherent system by [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-substitution-coherence]: it is natural under output restriction and coherent parameters, and for composable operators it identifies total composition with outputwise substitution, including identities, permutations, nullary blocks, discarded inputs, and all higher simplices. The assumed fiber Segal equivalence supplies the tuple products, while the chosen inert transport frame supplies the required cocartesian projection triangles.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7; Definition 2.1.1.10(1)-(3), especially its mapping-space condition; Remark 2.1.1.14. The relative mapping-space calculation is written out here.

proof.text: For a section $s$, its inert projections identify $s(\mathbf c)$ with $X_{\mathbf c}$, where $x_c=s(c)$. For an active one-output operator $\theta$, choose a $q$-cocartesian lift $u_\theta:X_{\mathbf c}\to T_\theta(X_{\mathbf c})$. The section edge $s(\theta)$ corresponds to a vertical arrow $a_\theta:T_\theta(X_{\mathbf c})\to x_d$ under the mapping-fiber equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] with parameter $\Delta^0$: it is characterized by a triangle $a_\theta u_\theta\simeq s(\theta)$ over $\theta$. Thus one factors the active edge through its active transport; one does not compose it with an inert transport to obtain $a_\theta$. That theorem applies because $q$ is an inner fibration with cocartesian lifts, and [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies its horn and mapping-square notions. Identity operators use the degenerate lift, and substitution uses the composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Inert operators give the corresponding cocartesian projection edges; permutations are the inert bijective case. Apply the pointwise transport theorem with each simplex or coherence-parameter shape to factor the triangles and their higher simplices together. This gives the specified coherent operation data, not just its images in homotopy categories.

source.place: Definition 2.1.3.1, together with cocartesian factorization (HTT 2.4.4.2-3, duals, carried by the cited pointwise-transport node).

proof.text: Here is the combinatorial meaning of the supplied all-higher tree data used in the converse. A simplex of $B$ is a chain $\mathbf c^0\xrightarrow{f_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{f_m}\mathbf c^m$. At level $a$ place a vertex labeled by $\theta_{a,j}$ at each output $j$ of $f_a$, and attach its input wires to the preceding level. This is a leveled forest, not in general a single rooted tree. A wire sent to the basepoint stops at that level. Keep the forests of every subinterval of levels as well: an operation performed before its output is discarded must still appear on the earlier face. For each interval $[a,b]$ and each nonempty output wire at level $b$, its ancestors give one rooted operation tree, and the mapping-space Segal decomposition of step 1 gives the product of its output-tree data. The missing output product is terminal. An internal face composes two adjacent $f_a$ and substitutes at the corresponding adjacent vertices; the initial and final faces remove the first and last levels; a degeneracy inserts unary identities on the wires. Reordering wires is the given permutation action. These descriptions also apply to nullary vertices. For a precise model retaining all higher compatibilities, use [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]: $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m](a,b)=N(P_{a,b})$, where $P_{a,b}$ is the poset of subsets of $\{a,\ldots,b\}$ containing the endpoints. A subset specifies the cuts at which the interval is evaluated in stages, refinement specifies the comparison, and a chain of refinements specifies its higher comparison simplex. Composition is union of subsets, hence grafting of the subinterval forests. The tree contractions, their chains, grafting and unary-identity data required in the statement are exactly these comparisons after taking the output products. In particular this dictionary includes comparisons involving a discarded branch on a proper face, although that branch contributes nothing to the final composite.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7 and Example 2.1.1.21; explicit agent-written leveled-forest and cut-poset expansion. Coherent-realization formula from the cited coherent-nerve node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-equivalence-lift] to $p=q$. The total and base simplicial sets are quasicategories, and $q$ is an inner fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Thus every $q$-cocartesian lift of a base equivalence is an equivalence in $E^\otimes$.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Definition 2.1.3.1; agent-written coherent assembly using the cited cut-poset nerve model and space-limit calculus.

proof.text: Because $q$ is a cocartesian fibration, it supplies lifts of every base equivalence; step 5 makes them equivalences, so the inner fibration $q$ is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Apply [lem-coef-relative-cut-nerve-diagrams] with $S=B$, $b=1_B$ and the tuple representatives of step 1. Its relative presentation computes actual sections with the chosen vertex identifications, rather than unrelated choices in separate homotopy categories.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Definition 2.1.3.1; agent-written coherent assembly using the cited cut-poset nerve model and space-limit calculus.

proof.text: In that presentation an interval cut specifies staged evaluation of the corresponding subinterval forest from step 4. Each chain of refinements specifies its comparison simplex. Replace each relative mapping space by the product of its output factors using step 1. This is an equivalence of complete comparison systems, not just of isolated spaces: on faces use the same restricted operators; on a union of cuts use substitution of the same vertex operations. The substitution-coherence statement [lem-coef-relative-operadic-output-substitution-coherence] and the coherent composition of transports in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identify these comparisons on all higher relations. Step 4's interval-forest dictionary identifies the output system with the supplied tree and pruning data of [def-coef-colored-operator-systems]. Discarded branches remain on the proper interval faces; empty final output gives the terminal product. Invariance of derived compatible-map spaces in [lem-coef-relative-cut-nerve-diagrams] therefore makes the map from total-arrow systems to output systems an equivalence. Its homotopy fiber at the supplied data is nonempty and contractible, since a quasi-inverse identifies such a fiber with a path space having one endpoint fixed and the other free. Choose a point in that fiber; it supplies a coherent section with all its specified comparison simplices. Its inert edges are cocartesian by the prescribed inert data. Only spaces of comparison data enter this derived construction; no limits in $E_c$ are needed.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2), Definition 2.1.3.1; agent-written coherent assembly using the cited cut-poset nerve model and space-limit calculus.

proof.text: Extraction followed by assembly is inverse with its identifications. On each color the comparison is the chosen identification of $X_{(c)}$ with $x_c$; on every operator its output factors are the supplied structure arrows by the defining homotopy fiber of step 7. On an arbitrary tuple the comparison is the inverse of the inert product equivalence, so it is an equivalence, including the empty tuple. There is no independent choice on a transport lift: [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes any such lift initial in $L(X,f)$, and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that the nonempty full category of initial objects is a contractible Kan complex. The higher comparisons of the inverse constructions are those in the homotopy fiber of the limit equivalence of step 7, so they agree on faces, degeneracies and grafting. This is why initiality of separate lifts alone would not have sufficed. Conversely, assembling and then extracting returns the supplied operation data with its specified tree comparisons. A homotopy fiber of an equivalence of spaces is contractible: a quasi-inverse identifies the fiber over $d$ with the space of a point equipped with a path to $d$, which contracts to the constant path. Thus the space of reconstructions together with an identification with the supplied data is contractible.

source.place: Definition 2.1.3.1; contractibility follows from the relative comparison constructed in steps 1-4 and the cited initial-object calculus.

proof.text: To include transformations and higher simplices, perform the construction with a parameter $K$ and base functors constant in the $K$ direction. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], $q_K:\operatorname{Fun}(K,E^\otimes)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$ is a cocartesian fibration, with cocartesian edges detected at vertices, and its fiber at the constant tuple $\mathbf c$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_{\mathbf c})$. The definition of the functor simplicial set in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\prod_iE_{c_i})=\prod_i\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_{c_i})$ degreewise. Postcomposition by a quasi-inverse of the tuple equivalence gives the corresponding equivalence for $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_{\mathbf c})$. Step 3's factorization now applies to coherent transformations of $K$-diagrams. In steps 4-7 replace every comparison shape by its product with $K$; faces, degeneracies and union of cuts act on the forest coordinate, while restriction in $K$ acts on the parameter coordinate, so the two commute. The space-limit argument retains all these mixed simplices. In particular $K=\Delta^1$ gives precisely the color maps and operation-naturality simplices of a transformation, and $K=\Delta^n$ gives every higher simplex and its restrictions. The two inverse comparisons in step 8 therefore give coherent natural equivalences of functors on the entire categories of data and sections. They are equivalences by the componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. This proves an equivalence of infinity-categories, rather than only an equivalence of their object spaces. No condition on $K$ beyond smallness in the chosen sufficiently large universe is used.

source.place: Remark 2.1.3.4 (parameter categories and pointwise operations), with the explicit exponential and cocartesian-transport argument above.

proof.text: Finally a simplicial map $K'\to K$ restricts each color diagram, each operation arrow and each comparison simplex by precomposition; the forest formulas do exactly the same precomposition. A suboperad restricts the list of colors and operation labels and hence the chains and cut diagrams. Projection to selected colors is evaluation at those one-term tuples. In all three cases the object, operator, face and cut formulas in steps 1-9 agree after restriction; their identification spaces are the same restricted homotopy fibers. This gives the claimed coherent naturality. The only products of objects used are the Segal identifications assumed in the statement, and the remaining limits are spaces of coherence choices, so there is no limit, colimit or presentability hypothesis on the fibers.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7, Definition 2.1.3.1 and Remark 2.1.3.4; explicit restriction of the constructed formulas.

proof_origin.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison before the inverse limit; supporting coherent operadic foundation. Detailed forest/cut-poset assembly is agent-written from the existing Segal, coherent-nerve and cocartesian-transport statements, with Higher Algebra places checked online in the 2017 edition.
